Roles/Permissions and Main Workflows name exact suite filenames per stream. No vocabulary, actor, state, input, or output gap was found that would let two implementers reasonably build different behavior, aside from the batch-composition inconsistency captured under CONTRADICTION (a direct textual conflict, not a vagueness issue).

requirements.md contains a direct, repeated (4-location) contradiction about which streams' edits belong to 'the ONE shared staged batch' for the R-10-protected `.github/workflows/test.yml`. Four passages state the batch contains only Streams A, B, and D: Non-goals' opening sentence ('That single batch carries: one CI step per new suite from Stream A AND from Stream B ... plus Stream D's step-prefix restructuring'); Roles and Permissions - Agent ('the ONE shared staged batch: Stream A's and Stream B's new CI steps plus Stream D's step-prefix lane marking'); Main Workflows item 4/Stream D ('together with Stream A's and Stream B's CI-step additions'); Security Boundaries row B3 ('the ONE shared staged batch (Streams A's/B's new CI steps and Stream D's step-prefix lane marking)'); and Risks 'Medium' ('Streams A, B, and D all stage edits ... carry all three streams' edits coherently'). Four other passages state the SAME batch contains Stream C too: Non-goals' later sentences ('Stream C registers its runner ... inside this ONE shared batch'), Roles and Permissions - CI ('the ONE shared staged `test.yml` candidate (Streams A + B + C + D)'), Main Workflows item 3/Stream C, and Open Questions OQ-4's resolution ('the ONE shared staged batch (Non-goals) carries Streams A/B/C/D's `test.yml` edits'). acceptance-tests.md AC-020 is unambiguous on this point: 'staged `.github/workflows/test.yml` candidate (the ONE shared batch, Streams A + B + C + D) contains a CI step for each new suite from AC-019.' Downstream failure: an agent or design reviewer who follows the Roles and Permissions 'Agent' bullet or the Security Boundaries B3 trust-boundary row literally (both explicitly enumerate only Streams A/B/D) would author a staged candidate omitting Stream C's `workflow-scenarios.tests.sh` CI step, directly violating AC-020 and reproducing exactly the silent-CI-skip gap (INV-006) this feature exists to close. This is a same-document internal-consistency defect over a protected-file scope boundary, squarely a spec-review-stage issue since design.md's own Global Constraints is tasked only with ordering edits 'WITHIN that single batch' and cannot do so correctly while the batch's membership is stated inconsistently in the source document.

requirements.md's Edge Cases section enumerates fail-closed uniformity across every new negative case (AC-005/008/009/010), a false-negative guard for PATH-restriction fixtures, PowerShell-stub non-functionality tolerance paired with an independent real-interpreter parity check, explicit cross-runtime/OS-independence discipline, ADR-0010 blocker re-check timing, and Stream D's step-drop/needs-list-change risk with a required enumerate-and-confirm self-check. acceptance-tests.md operationalizes each into named boundary/negative TEST IDs: TEST-005's 2 required sub-cases for the all-absent fail-closed path, TEST-008/009/010's 12-combination matrices (TEST-010 additionally adds a false-DENY control sub-case), TEST-017's literal RED-then-GREEN dropped-step proof, and TEST-018's non-regression check for isolated workflow files. No material negative path, empty state, boundary condition, or failure mode implied by the four streams' requirements was found without a corresponding acceptance test.

The Assumptions section's five entries are each either resolved with a cited current-state fact re-verified at spec-authoring time (identity-ledger tail sequence 337; ADR-0010 `Status: Accepted` at commit `67015a5`) or explicitly marked for RE-VERIFY at implementation time under the named WFI-013 discipline (registration-gap state for 4 named suites; `PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES`/`PHASE2_HUMAN_COPY_TARGETS` membership; `loop-driver.sh`'s spec-only stage scope; `collection-layer.tests.sh`'s PATH technique) rather than left as silent, unstated premises. The human-copy staging boundary for the R-10-protected `.github/workflows/test.yml` is in scope and testable: Roles and Permissions names the human maintainer as the sole party who validates and applies the staged candidate as a pre-merge commit; AC-016/AC-020 require the change to be staged under `specs/epic-136-phase3/human-copy/` with a `MANIFEST.sha256` (never written live by the agent) and require the live file's self-check to remain red until the human applies it ('no staged-candidate fallback'). ADR-0010's own human-governance decision is cited as already made and closed (commit `67015a5`), not an open boundary requiring further spec definition. This boundary is well-defined and verifiable independent of the batch-composition contradiction noted under CONTRADICTION.

The same batch-composition contradiction identified under CONTRADICTION forces a design reviewer to invent a scope decision rather than receive one: requirements.md explicitly tasks design.md's Global Constraints with resolving 'only the internal ordering of these edits WITHIN that single batch,' but the document gives two irreconcilable answers to 'what is in that batch' (3 streams per Roles and Permissions - Agent / Security Boundaries B3 / Risks-Medium, vs. 4 streams per Roles and Permissions - CI / Non-goals / OQ-4 / acceptance-tests.md AC-020). A design reviewer treating the Roles and Permissions or Security Boundaries sections as authoritative (both plausible, load-bearing sections) would produce an ordering plan that never accounts for Stream C's edit, since it cannot decide which of the conflicting statements to trust without inventing the resolution itself -- exactly the missing-product-behavior gap this check exists to catch before implementation-policy review.
